Queen Victoria: Victoria was the daughter of Prince Edward, Duke of Kent and Strathearn (the fourth son of King George III), and Princess Victoria of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld.

Edward VII: As Prince of Wales, Edward travelled throughout Britain performing ceremonial public duties and represented Britain on visits abroad.

Lutheranism: The Lutheran churches adhere to the Bible and the ecumenical creeds, with Lutheran doctrine being explicated in the Book of Concord.
House of Orange-Nassau: William the Silent. Several members of the house served during the Eighty Years' War and after as stadtholder ("governor"; Dutch: stadhouder) during the Dutch Republic.

East India Company: John Watts. The East India Company (EIC) was an English, and later British, joint-stock company that was founded in 1600 and dissolved in 1874.
In which country is Fall of Kabul (2021)?
Fall of Kabul (2021): Afghanistan. On 15 August 2021, Afghanistan's capital city of Kabul was captured by the Taliban after a major insurgent offensive that began in May 2021.
In which country is Free Cause Party based?
Free Cause Party: Turkey. The Free Cause Party (Turkish: Hür Dava Partisi, HÜDA PAR; Kurdish: Partiya Doza Azad) is a Kurdish Sunni Islamist political party in Turkey.

Battle of Kiev (1941): Ukraine. The battle lasted from 7 July to 26 September 1941 as part of Operation Barbarossa, the Axis invasion of the Soviet Union.

In which country is Janata Party based?
Janata Party: India. The Janata Party (JP, lit. 'People's Party') is an unrecognised political party in India.
In which country did the Battle of the Pyramids take place?
Battle of the Pyramids: Egypt. Occurring near the village of Embabeh, Ottoman Egypt, the battle was named by Napoleon after the distant Great Pyramid of Giza.
Babylonia: Iraq. It emerged as an Akkadian-populated but Amorite-ruled state c. 1894 BC.
In which country is Finns Party based?
Finns Party: Finland. It was founded in 1995 following the dissolution of the Finnish Rural Party.
In which country is Interpol based?
Interpol: France. It is the world's largest international police organization.
Which of these was an official language of the Novgorod Republic?
Novgorod Republic: Old East Slavic. For much of its history, Novgorod was the center of Russian art and culture.
Which of these was an official language of Sheba?
Sheba: Sabaean. Sheba, or Saba, was an ancient South Arabian kingdom that existed in Yemen before 275 CE.
Which of these was an official language of the Kingdom of Jerusalem?
Kingdom of Jerusalem: Latin. The Kingdom of Jerusalem, also known as the Crusader Kingdom, was one of the Crusader states established in the Levant immediately after the First Crusade.
Of which country was Sanskrit an official language?

Sanskrit is an official language of Gupta Empire. The Gupta Empire was an Indian empire during the classical period of the Indian subcontinent which existed from the mid 3rd century to mid 6th century CE.
The son of a Trojan prince and the goddess Aphrodite, this mythological hero appears only briefly in Homer's Iliad but receives an entire Roman epic devoted to his journey — who is he?
Aeneas (in-; Classical; from Ancient) was a Trojan hero in Greco-Roman mythology, the son of the Trojan prince Anchises and the Greek goddess Aphrodite (equivalent to the Roman Venus).
She has led the AfD's parliamentary group in the Bundestag since 2017 and now co-chairs the party with Tino Chrupalla — which German politician is it?

Alice Weidel (born 6 February 1979) is a German far-right politician who has been serving as co-chairwoman of the far-right, vlkisch nationalist Alternative for Germany (AfD) party alongside Tino Chrupalla since June 2022.
A career diplomat who advocated for the 2003 invasion of Iraq, this man went on to serve as the 71st U.S. secretary of state from 2021 to 2025 — who is he?
Antony Blinken (born April 16, 1962) is an American lawyer and diplomat who served as the 71st United States secretary of state from 2021 to 2025.

Originally depicted as a lioness, this ancient Egyptian goddess was later associated with the domestic cat and worshipped as early as 2890 BCE, sharing a dual nature with the warrior goddess Sekhmet — who is she?
Bastet (Ancient), also known as Ubasti or Bubastis, is a goddess of ancient Egyptian religion, possibly of Nubian origin, worshipped as early as the Second Dynasty (2890 BCE).
Believed to have once been an NKVD informant, this Polish communist led his country from 1948 to 1956 and imposed the Stalinist system there — who was he?
Bolesław Bierut (18 April 1892 - 12 March 1956) was a Polish communist activist and politician who was the leader of communist-ruled Poland from 1948 until 1956.

Eton-educated and aristocratic, this British general is best remembered for his 1781 surrender at Yorktown — yet he later governed both Ireland and India, where his name lives on in a famous legal code. Who was he?
Charles Cornwallis, 1st Marquess Cornwallis (31 December 1738 - 5 October 1805) was a British Army officer, Whig politician and colonial administrator.
This immensely wealthy final king of Lydia fell to Cyrus the Great after the fall of his capital, Sardis, in the 6th century BC — who was he?
Croesus (Ancient) was the last king of Lydia from 585 BC to 546 BC.
After a term as Russia's president, he swapped chairs to become prime minister from 2012 to 2020, and now serves as deputy chairman of the Security Council — which Russian politician is this?
Dmitry Medvedev (born 14 September 1965) is a Russian politician and lawyer who served as the president of Russia from 2008 to 2012 and as the prime minister of Russia from 2012 to 2020.
Dubbed the 'Father of the Nation' and also a noted historian behind the book Capitalism and Slavery, this leader steered Trinidad and Tobago to independence — who is it?
Eric Williams (25 September 1911 - 29 March 1981) was a Trinidad and Tobago politician.

This Dutch politician served as First Vice-President of the European Commission under Jean-Claude Juncker, later became the EU's climate action commissioner, and then led a Dutch political alliance in parliament from 2023 to 2025. Who is he?
Frans Timmermans (born 6 May 1961) is a Dutch politician who was the leader of GroenLinks-PvdA in the House of Representatives from 2023 to 2025.
Working alongside Simone de Beauvoir to expose torture during the Algerian War, this feminist lawyer later signed a landmark 1971 declaration demanding free abortion access — who is she?
Gisèle Halimi (born Zeiza Gisle lise Taeb,; 27 July 1927 - 28 July 2020) was a Tunisian-French lawyer, politician, essayist and feminist activist.
As China's top leader on Hong Kong and Macau affairs, this former Shanghai mayor rose to the Politburo Standing Committee before becoming vice president in 2023 — who is he?
Han Zheng (pinyin: Hn Zhng; born April 1955) is a Chinese politician who, since 2023, has served as the 11th vice president of China.
Dated to begin about 5,200 years ago with the invention of writing, this scholarly record traces humanity's religious feelings, thoughts, and ideas across the millennia — what field of study is this?
History of religion is the written record of human religious feelings, thoughts, and ideas.
A professor of Ukrainian language and a nationalist member of parliament from 2012 to 2014, this linguist campaigned hard for heritage-language learning - who is she?
Iryna Farion (29 April 1964 - 19 July 2024) was a Ukrainian linguist and nationalist politician who served as a deputy in the Verkhovna Rada from 2012 to 2014.

Elected New York's first female county judge and later county district attorney, this Lebanese-American TV host and lawyer has served as the U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia since May 2025. Who is she?
Jeanine Pirro (born June 2, 1951) is a Lebanese-American television host, lawyer, and author who has been serving as the United States attorney for the District of Columbia since May 2025.
This Nova Scotian-born seaman turned his record-setting solo voyage aboard the Spray into the best-seller "Sailing Alone Around the World" — who was he?
Joshua Slocum (February 20, 1844 - on or shortly after November 14, 1909) was the first person to sail single-handedly around the world.
Commander of the Tobruk-based Libyan National Army, this officer has been the de facto ruler of eastern Libya since 2017, governing it as a military dictatorship. Who is he?
Khalifa Haftar (born 7 November 1943) is a Libyan politician, military officer, and the commander of the Tobruk-based Libyan National Army (LNA).
Born Lev Bronstein, this Marxist theorist stood with Lenin as one of the two most prominent figures of the early Soviet state — until he was exiled in 1929 and assassinated in 1940. Who was he?
Leon Trotsky was Soviet politician and revolutionary (1879–1940).
Chancellor of a university in Haryana and MLA for Tijara in Rajasthan, this politician also serves as the eighth head of a Hindu monastic sect — who is he?
Mahant Balaknath (born 16 April 1984) is an Indian politician and current MLA from Tijara constituency in Rajasthan.
This French politician has led the La France Insoumise parliamentary group in the National Assembly since 2021, having represented a Val-de-Marne constituency since 2017 — who is she?
Mathilde Panot (French; born 15 January 1989) is a French politician who has served as the president of the La France Insoumise group in the National Assembly since October 2021.
This Roman goddess of wisdom and strategic warfare shared the Capitoline Triad with Jupiter and Juno, and is often shown with an owl — who is she?
Minerva is the Roman goddess of wisdom, justice, law, victory, and the sponsor of arts, trade, and strategy.
While 'nudism' stresses the practice itself, this near-synonym highlights an attitude of harmony with nature woven into non-sexual social nudity — which term?
Naturism is a lifestyle of practicing non-sexual social nudity in private and in public; the word also refers to the cultural movement which advocates and defends that lifestyle.
Marked by financial and personal failure before 1640, this English soldier rose to lead Parliament's army, championed the execution of Charles I, and ruled as Lord Protector. Who is he?
Oliver Cromwell (25 April 1599 - 3 September 1658) was an English statesman, farmer and soldier, widely regarded as one of the most important figures in British history.
This historical region in southwestern Iran, corresponding to Fars province, saw Iranic-speaking migrants arrive from Central Asia in ancient times — what is it called?
Persis is a historical region in south-western Iran, roughly corresponding with Fars province.

Officially known as the Religious Society of Friends, members of this Christian movement got their popular nickname after founder George Fox told a judge to 'quake before the authority of God' — what are they called?
Quakers are people who belong to the Religious Society of Friends, originally known as simply the Society of Friends, a historically Protestant Christian set of denominations.
A decorated Vietnam Marine awarded a Bronze Star and Purple Heart, he led the FBI as its sixth director from 2001 to 2013 after appointments under presidents of both parties. Who?
Robert Mueller (August 7, 1944 - March 20, 2026) was an American lawyer who served as the sixth director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) from 2001 to 2013.

Widely expected to succeed his mother as India's prime minister, this politician's sudden death in a 1980 plane crash instead paved the way for his older brother to inherit that political legacy — who was he?
Sanjay Gandhi (14 December 1946 - 23 June 1980) was an Indian politician.

This Yugoslav and Serbian politician served as president of Serbia (1989–1997) and then the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (1997–2000). He was the first sitting head of state charged with war crimes. Who is he?

Slobodan Milošević (Serbian) was a Yugoslav and Serbian politician who was the president of Serbia between 1989 and 1997 and president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia from 1997 until his overthrow in 2000.
With an unclassified script of just 97 known inscriptions, this Bronze Age Iberian culture is considered the first named kingdom of southwestern Spain — which civilization?
Tartessos is, as defined by archaeological discoveries, a historical civilization settled in the southern Iberian Peninsula from about the late Bronze Age until the 5th century BC.

Led by Gamal Abdel Nasser, this short-lived political union between Egypt and Syria existed from 1958 until Syria seceded following a 1961 coup, with Egypt keeping the joint name until 1971 — what was this country called?
United Arab Republic was a country and sovereign state in the Middle East from 1958 to 1971.
After forcing the last Qing emperor's abdication and later dying in 1916, Yuan Shikai left behind a power vacuum that split China among competing military strongmen — which turbulent period followed?

Warlord Era was the period in the history of the Republic of China between 1916 and 1928, when control of the country was divided between rival military cliques of the Beiyang Army and other regional factions.

A longtime Communist Party member and labour lawyer, this Spanish politician founded an electoral alliance in 2023 while serving as her country's Minister of Labour and Second Deputy Prime Minister — who is she?

Yolanda Díaz (born 6 May 1971) is a Spanish politician and labour lawyer, currently serving as Second Deputy Prime Minister since 2021, and Minister of Labour and Social Economy of the Government of Spain since 2020.
Serving briefly as prime minister before becoming Turkey's president from 2007 to 2014, he earlier joined forces with a fellow reformist named Erdoğan after his party split in 2000 — who is he?
Abdullah Gül: President of Turkey from 2007 to 2014. Abdullah Gül (born 29 October 1950) is a Turkish politician who served as the president of Turkey from 2007 to 2014.
A poet and politician from Martinique, he coined the very word "négritude," served decades in the French National Assembly, and was mayor of Fort-de-France for 56 years. Who was he?
Aimé Césaire: Martinican writer, poet and politician (1913–2008)

Alfonso VI of León and Castile

Alfonso VI of León and Castile

On Interpol's top-10 most-wanted list for robberies in the 1970s and '80s, this Serbian warlord later led the feared Serb Volunteer Guard through the Yugoslav Wars — by what single name was he known?
Arkan: Serbian paramilitary commander and mobster (1952–2000)
Leading a 'joyous religion' freedom movement from a base in Azerbaijan, this Iranian rebel fought the Abbasid Caliphate for over two decades before being betrayed and killed in 838 — who was he?

This pair of Depression-era outlaws travelled the central United States with their gang until both were killed on the same day. In which year?
Bonnie Elizabeth Parker (1910-1934) and Clyde Chestnut Barrow (1909-1934) were outlaws who travelled the Central United States with their gang. Both died on 23 May 1934.
A Corsican attorney who once fought for the island's independence, this nobleman is remembered chiefly as the father of history's most famous French emperor — who was he?
Carlo Buonaparte: Father of Napoleon Bonaparte (1746–1785)
A New York Republican who became the 21st president after Garfield's assassination, he oversaw the largest expansion of the US Navy and the end of the "spoils system." Who was he?
Chester A. Arthur: President of the United States from 1881 to 1885.
Emphasizing virtues like benevolence, righteousness and propriety, this Chinese school of thought emerged around 500 BCE from the teachings of a sage whose name it bears — what is it called?
Confucianism: Chinese ethical and philosophical system.
Born Deedar Randhawa, which Indian wrestler beat Lou Thesz to become world champion in 1968, later playing Hanuman on screen and entering the WWE Hall of Fame?
Dara Singh: Indian professional wrestler and actor (1928–2012)

As a longtime confidant who followed his boss from Shanghai to Beijing, this Chinese official now serves as the country's top-ranked vice premier and sixth-ranked member of the Communist Party's Politburo Standing Committee — who is he?
Ding Xuexiang: First-ranking Vice Premier of China since 2023.

Ushered in by a decisive 1600 battlefield victory and a shogun title granted by the emperor, this roughly 260-year era of Japanese history brought prolonged peace, strict social order, and a flourishing of arts under isolationist rule — which era is it?
Edo period: Japanese history from 1600 to 1868.
In 1932, Australian artillery soldiers armed with Lewis guns were deployed against crop-raiding flightless birds in Western Australia — and lost. What did the media dub this campaign?
Emu War: 1932 Australian nuisance wildlife management campaign.
Formed in 1980 from four merged Salvadoran guerrilla groups, this left-wing party fought the government throughout a civil war that lasted until 1992 — which group?
Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front: Salvadoran political party and former guerilla organization.
The 32nd US president who served from 1933 until his death in 1945, the longest-serving and only one to serve more than two terms—who was he?
Franklin D. Roosevelt: President of the United States from 1933 to 1945.
Beginning on 7 October 2023 with a surprise attack that killed 1,195 people and took 251 hostages, this conflict has since claimed over 73,000 Palestinian lives — what is it?
Gaza war: Ongoing armed conflict in the Middle East.

Rising to prominence during Greece's government-debt crisis, this far-right, neo-Nazi organization became the third-largest party in the Greek parliament following the January 2015 election, before its support collapsed — which group?
Golden Dawn (Greece): Greek neo-Nazi criminal organisation.
According to Genesis, this Egyptian woman bore Abraham's firstborn son, Ishmael, and though unnamed in the Quran, Islam regards her as his second wife — who is she?
A German general and military theorist, he pioneered the 'blitzkrieg' approach and was central to developing the panzer division concept and tank warfare — who was he?
Heinz Guderian: German Wehrmacht Heer general (1888–1954)
Founded in Jordanian-controlled Jerusalem in 1953 by a Palestinian religious-court judge, this pan-Islamist group seeks to reestablish a global caliphate under sharia — which organization?

Hizb ut-Tahrir: Pan-Islamist and fundamentalist organization. The organization sees world history as an eternal conflict between Islam and non-believers, with the state system considered a historical assault on Islam.
Known for fiery anti-Catholic sermons, this Northern Irish loyalist co-founded the Free Presbyterian Church of Ulster and led the DUP from 1971 — who is it?
Ian Paisley: Northern Irish politician and religious leader (1926–2014)

Also known by the acronym Daesh, this jihadist militant group declared a worldwide caliphate in 2014 and at its peak controlled territory in Iraq and Syria home to about 12 million people — which organization?
Islamic State: Salafi jihadist militant organisation.
The last Founding Father to reach the White House, this president of the "Era of Good Feelings" issued a famous doctrine warning Europe off the Americas — who was he?
James Monroe: Founding Father, U.S. president from 1817 to 1825.
A well-traveled businessman who lent his villa for the secret 1933 talks that made Hitler chancellor, he became Nazi Germany's foreign minister — and a war criminal. Who was he?
Joachim von Ribbentrop: German politician and diplomat (1893–1946)
Starting in 1950, this Wisconsin senator became the face of America's red-scare panic, alleging communists had infiltrated the government, until the Senate censured him in 1954 — who was he?
Descended from Oghuz Turks and centered in south-central Anatolia, this Turkish principality was one of the most powerful in the region until its fall in 1487 — which dynasty?
Karamanids: 1250–1487 Turkish beylik in south-central Anatolia.
Nicknamed 'the Balkan Prussia' for its frequent wars, this Southeastern European tsardom was proclaimed in 1908 when Prince Ferdinand raised it from a principality — what state was it?
Kingdom of Bulgaria: State in southeastern Europe from 1908 to 1946.

After the Moscow Armistice forced Finland to break ties with Germany in September 1944, fighting broke out in Finland's northernmost region as German troops withdrew toward occupied Norway — what's this conflict called?
Lapland War: 1944–1945 war between Finland and Germany.
Fought from 1558 to 1583 over present-day Estonia and Latvia, this conflict pitted Russia against a shifting coalition of Sweden, Denmark-Norway, and Poland-Lithuania — which conflict?
Livonian War: 16th-century war in Eastern Europe.

Born to a Berber family in what's now Algeria, he became the first Roman emperor from outside the senatorial class — and the first to never once set foot in Rome during his reign, after conspiring to have Caracalla murdered. Who was he?
Known as 'the richest man in Rome,' this general crushed the slave revolt led by Spartacus and later joined Caesar and Pompey in an unofficial ruling alliance — who was he?
Marcus Licinius Crassus: Roman general and statesman (115–53 BC)
Nicknamed "The Flying Finn," this ski jumper won four Olympic golds — three of them at a single 1988 Games — making him one of the sport's greatest ever. Who was he?
Before becoming the 70th U.S. secretary of state under Donald Trump, this Kansas congressman led the CIA and graduated from West Point in 1986 — who is he?
Mike Pompeo: American politician and diplomat (born 1963)

At the 1997 Survivor Series, a referee secretly helped WWF owner Vince McMahon alter the outcome of a championship match, costing Bret Hart the title without his knowledge — what is this incident known as?
Revered for freeing his kingdom from vassalage to the Toungoo Empire, this Ayutthaya monarch ruled from 1590 and later welcomed Dutch traders — who is he?
Naresuan: King of Siam from 1590 to 1605.
Consisting of right view, right speech, and six other 'right' practices, this early Buddhist teaching charts the way toward liberation from the cycle of rebirth — what is it called?
Noble Eightfold Path: Buddhist practices leading to liberation from saṃsāra.
After resigning as Germany's finance minister within six months of taking office, this politician later co-founded a left-wing party opposing his former party's reforms — who is he?
Forced out of school at ten by poverty, this future Chinese general rose from private second class to become Minister of National Defense from 1954 to 1959 — who was he?
Peng Dehuai: Chinese politician and general (1898–1974)
This ancient Indian king fought valiantly against Alexander the Great at the Battle of the Hydaspes in 326 BC, and was rewarded with an expanded realm despite his defeat — who is he?
Before serving as Chicago's mayor and later as U.S. ambassador to Japan, this Illinois Democrat was Barack Obama's first White House chief of staff — who is he?
Rahm Emanuel: American politician and diplomat (born 1959)

This American naval aviator and polar explorer discovered Mount Sidley — Antarctica's largest dormant volcano — and claimed to be first to reach both Poles by air, though the North Pole claim remains disputed. Who was he?
Richard E. Byrd: American naval officer (1888–1957)
This August 1992 siege in Boundary County, Idaho began when U.S. Marshals came to arrest Randy Weaver — over a sawed-off shotgun sale — after he was given the wrong court date. What event was it?
Ruby Ridge standoff: 1992 siege and shootout in Idaho, US.
A former partisan and socialist politician, this journalist-turned-statesman served as president of Italy from 1978 to 1985 — who is he?
Sandro Pertini: President of Italy from 1978 to 1985.
At 35, he became Russia's youngest-ever prime minister in 1998 and later ran the Rosatom nuclear agency for over a decade — who is this Kremlin technocrat?
Sergey Kiriyenko: Prime Minister of Russia In 1998.
This king moved Poland's capital from Kraków to Warsaw and was the first Polish monarch from a Swedish royal house — who is he?
Sigismund III Vasa: King of Poland and Grand Duke of Lithuania (1587–1632), King of Sweden (1592–1599)
Crowned in 1576 after marrying Queen Anna Jagiellon, this ruler defeated a rival claimant to become the third elected king of Poland — who was he?
Stephen Báthory: Ruler of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth from 1576 to 1586.
A teacher, Marxist, and philosopher honored as a "Father of the Republic of Indonesia," this independence fighter founded the Murba Party and lived the life of a guerrilla and spy — who was he?
Tan Malaka: Indonesian communist philosopher, activist, and national hero (1897–1949)
This Norwegian adventurer drifted 8,000 km across the Pacific on a hand-built raft in 1947 to test his theory that South Americans settled Polynesia first — who is he?
Thor Heyerdahl: Norwegian anthropologist and adventurer (1914–2002)
This Indian politician served as Maharashtra's 19th chief minister from 2019 to 2022 while also editing a newspaper for over a decade — who is he?
Uddhav Thackeray: 19th Chief Minister of Maharashtra from 2019 to 2022 (born 1960)

Raiding, trading, and settling from Scandinavia across Europe, North Africa, and even Newfoundland between the late 8th and 11th centuries, this seafaring people helped establish Kievan Rus'. Who were they?
Vikings: Norse seafarers, merchants and raiders.
Launched by the United States after the September 11 attacks, this global campaign targeted al-Qaeda, the Taliban, and later Iraq's Ba'athist regime — what was it called?
War on terror: Military campaign following the September 11 attacks.
First achieved in Australasia before spreading to Europe and the Americas, this democratic right for female voters began its 'first wave' in 1893 in English-speaking countries — what right?
Women's suffrage: Legal right of women to vote.
Revered as the Father of the Nation, this ruler of Abu Dhabi became the first president of a newly unified Gulf federation in 1971?
Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan: President of the United Arab Emirates from 1971 to 2004.

What is the atomic number of Xenon?
Xenon is a chemical element; it has symbol Xe and atomic number 54.
What is the atomic number of Unbibium?
Unbibium, also known as element 122 or eka-thorium, is a hypothetical chemical element; it has placeholder symbol Ubb and atomic number 122.
In what year did Pythagoras die?
Pythagoras: Pythagoras of Samos (Ancient Greek: Πυθαγόρας; c. 570 – c. 495 BC) was an ancient Ionian Greek philosopher, polymath, and the eponymous founder of Pythagoreanism.
In what year was Kepler's Supernova discovered?
Kepler's Supernova: SN 1604, also known as Kepler's Supernova, Kepler's Nova or Kepler's Star, was a Type Ia supernova that occurred in the Milky Way, in the constellation Ophiuchus.
PHP: Rasmus Lerdorf. PHP is a general-purpose scripting language geared towards web development.
Which company manufactures KAI KF-21 Boramae?
KAI KF-21 Boramae: Korea Aerospace Industries. The KAI KF-21 Boramae (Korean: KF-21 보라매; lit. 'KF-21 Hunting Hawk'; formerly KF-X; commonly KF-21) is a South Korean twin-engine fighter aircraft.
Fufu: Ghana. Fufu (or fufuo, foofoo, foufou foo-foo) is a pounded meal found in West African cuisine.
Who is credited with discovering Tennessine?
Tennessine: Yuri Oganessian. Tennessine is a synthetic element; it has symbol Ts and atomic number 117.
Who is credited with discovering Ammonia?
Ammonia: Joseph Priestley. Ammonia is an inorganic chemical compound of nitrogen and hydrogen with the formula NH3.
Who is credited with discovering Selenium?
Selenium: Jöns Jacob Berzelius. Selenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Se and atomic number 34.
These large seabirds of the tubenose order range widely across the Southern Ocean and North Pacific, but are notably absent from the North Atlantic today. What birds are they?
Albatross are large seabirds related to the procellariids, storm petrels, and diving petrels in the order Procellariiformes (the tubenoses).
Closely related to Hepatica and Pulsatilla, which flowering plant genus in the buttercup family is nicknamed the windflower?
Anemone is a genus of flowering plants in the buttercup family Ranunculaceae.
With almost 500 species in the daisy family, this large plant genus includes mugwort, wormwood, and sagebrush, and is sometimes confused with a related genus of sages — which genus?
Artemisia (plant) (art--) is a large, diverse genus of plants belonging to the daisy family, Asteraceae, with almost 500 species.
Marketed early on as the Debonair in its conventional-tail form, this piston single has been built continuously longer than any other aircraft ever made — which model?
Beechcraft Bonanza is an American general aviation aircraft introduced in 1947 by Beech Aircraft Corporation of Wichita, Kansas.
Ranging from southern Canada down to Oaxaca, Mexico, this North American wild cat sports black bars on its forelegs and a short, bobbed tail. What animal is it?
Bobcat (Lynx rufus), also known as the wildcat, bay lynx, or red lynx, is one of the four extant species within the medium-sized wild cat genus Lynx.
This basic unit of digital information most often consists of eight bits, and is called an 'octet' in network protocol documents to avoid ambiguity. What is it?
Byte is a unit of digital information that most commonly consists of eight bits.
A flightless ratite native to the tropical forests of New Guinea and northeastern Australia, this large bird has three living species and lacks a keel on its breastbone — name the bird?
Cassowary (Tok) are flightless birds of the genus Casuarius, in the order Casuariiformes.

A long-term lung condition that makes breathing progressively harder due to damaged airways and lung tissue, this condition develops gradually and currently cannot be cured, though treatments and lifestyle changes help manage symptoms. What is this disease, commonly abbreviated?
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a long-term lung condition that makes it progressively harder to breathe.
This group of mostly evergreen, cone-bearing trees and shrubs reproduces via wind-pollination, with the seeds themselves also scattered by the wind — what plant group is it?
Conifer are a group of vascular plants and a subset of gymnosperms.
First created in 1994 and named for the German city where it was made, this synthetic element with atomic number 110 sits below platinum on the periodic table — what's it called?
Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.
Its name comes from the Ancient Greek for 'female dragon,' and this genus of roughly 200 tree and shrub species now also includes what was once classified as Sansevieria — which genus is it?
Dracaena (plant) is a genus of about 200-220 species of trees and woody shrubs.

Named for Latin words meaning 'within the cytoplasm' and 'little net,' this eukaryotic cell organelle handles protein folding and comes in rough and smooth varieties, forming an interconnected network of membrane-enclosed sacs — name this organelle?
Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a part of a transportation system of the eukaryotic cell, and has many other important functions such as protein folding.
Home to seven living cat species, from the tiny black-footed cat to the jungle cat, and the wild ancestor line of the housecat, which genus of felines is this?
Felis is a genus of small and medium-sized cat species native to most of Africa and south of 60 latitude in Europe and Asia to Indochina.

Heterotrophs like animals, members of this kingdom eat by secreting enzymes into their surroundings, and they get around mainly by simply growing — except for the occasional flagellated spore drifting through air or water. What group is it?
Fungus (pl.: fungi or funguses) is any member of the group of eukaryotic organisms that includes yeasts, molds, as well as mushrooms.
The largest living primate, with arm spans reaching 2.6 metres, this equatorial-African great ape shares up to 99% of its DNA with humans — what is it?
Gorilla are large, primarily herbivorous, great apes that live in the tropical forests of equatorial Africa.
In their healthy state these vascular cushions in the anal canal actually help with stool control — it's only when they swell or inflame that they earn the nickname "piles." What are they?
Hemorrhoid (or haemorrhoids), also known as piles, are vascular structures in the anal canal.
Behaviorally and physically dog-like despite being closer kin to felines, this carnivoran's family is the fifth-smallest in its order with only four extant species — what is it?
Hyena (hi-; from Ancient Greek, haina) are feliform carnivoran mammals belonging to the family Hyaenidae (Latin).

Also known by the old names green vitriol and copperas, this heptahydrate salt dissolves in water to form a paramagnetic, octahedral aquo complex and is used medically to fight anemia — which compound is it?
Iron(II) sulfate (British) denotes a range of salts with the formula FeSO4xH2O.

Nicknamed 'Marvellous Merchiston,' this Scottish laird and mathematician popularised the decimal point and invented a set of calculating 'bones' — but he's best known for discovering what underlies the slide rule. Who was he?
John Napier (Latinized as Ioannes Neper; 1 February 1550 - 4 April 1617), nicknamed Marvellous Merchiston, was a Scottish landowner known as a mathematician, physicist and astronomer.

This genus of rod-shaped, gram-positive bacteria forms a significant part of the human microbiota in places like the digestive and genital tracts, and until a 2020 taxonomic overhaul included 261 distinct species — what's the genus?
Lactobacillus is a genus of gram-positive bacteria within the Lactobacillaceae family.
This ACE inhibitor can take up to four weeks for full effect and is also used to prevent kidney problems in people with diabetes — which medication?
Lisinopril is a medication belonging to the drug class of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and is used to treat hypertension (high blood pressure), heart failure, and heart attacks.
Recognizable by the male's iridescent green head, this widespread dabbling duck species has been introduced to countries from New Zealand to South Africa far beyond its native range — what is it?
Mallard (Anas platyrhynchos) is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout the temperate and subtropical Americas, Eurasia, and North Africa.
Nicknamed "quicksilver," this is the only metallic element that stays liquid at room temperature, and it's often mined as the red mineral cinnabar — which element is it?
Mercury (element) is a chemical element; it has symbol Hg and atomic number 80.
Its English name passed from Greek to Latin to Portuguese before landing in English in the early 1600s — which family of roughly 200 marine fish species boasts 16 genera?
Moray eel are a family of eels whose members are found worldwide.
First linked by a Michigan doctor to farm wives sickened by isolation, this Gilded Age diagnosis grouped together fatigue, headaches, and a depressed mood — what condition?
Neurasthenia (from Ancient Greek (neuron) 'nerve' and (asthens) 'weak') is a term that was first used as early as 1829 for a mechanical weakness of the nerves.
In this learning process, voluntary behaviors grow more frequent through reinforcement or fade through punishment and extinction — what is it called?
Operant conditioning is a learning process in which voluntary behaviors are modified by association with the addition (or removal) of reward or aversive stimuli.
A physician in this medical field — devoted to the study of disease and diagnosing it largely by analyzing tissue and cell samples — is called a pathologist. What is the field?
Pathology is the study of disease. The word pathology also refers to the study of disease in general, incorporating a wide range of biology research fields and medical practices.
This branch of linguistics is concerned with how speech sounds are physically produced, transmitted as sound waves, and perceived by listeners — name the field?
Phonetics is a branch of linguistics that mainly concerns the articulation, sound wave properties, and perception of speech sounds.
Born Joseph Ratzinger in Bavaria, this pontiff led the Catholic Church from 2005 until an unusual resignation in 2013, after which he adopted an 'emeritus' title — who was he?
Pope Benedict XVI (born Joseph Alois Ratzinger; 16 April 1927 - 31 December 2022) was the head of the Catholic Church and sovereign of Vatican City from 2005 until his resignation in 2013.
Found in nucleic acids as the building block behind adenine and guanine, this nitrogen-rich heterocyclic compound is the most common of its kind in nature — what is it?
Purine is a heterocyclic aromatic organic compound that consists of two rings (pyrimidine and imidazole) fused together.
Home to about 200 species — among them the plants we call currants and gooseberries — this genus is the sole member of its own plant family — which genus?
Ribes is a genus of approximately 200 known species of flowering plants, predominantly native to the temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere.

This volatile, colorless, and odorless nerve agent is so potent a chemical weapon that inhaling a lethal dose can cause death from respiratory paralysis within one to ten minutes — what's the compound called?
Sarin (NATO designation GB short for G-series, B) is an extremely toxic organophosphorus compound that has been often used as a chemical weapon due to its extreme potency as a nerve agent.

Built for the Marine Corps by adding a third engine and a seventh main rotor blade to an earlier heavy-lift helicopter, this aircraft entered service in 1981 and flies from Navy ships — which helicopter?
Sikorsky CH-53E Super Stallion is a heavy lift helicopter operated by the United States military.
Members of the family Sciuridae, whose closest living relatives are surprisingly the mountain beaver and dormice, these rodents are native to the Americas, Eurasia and Africa — what are they called?
Squirrel (z)) are members of the family Sciuridae (sih-, -dee), a family that includes small or medium-sized rodents.

A leguminous tree bearing edible brown pod-like fruits with sweet, tangy pulp, indigenous to tropical Africa and naturalized in Asia, its wood and seed oil have varied uses from cuisine to traditional medicine. What is this tree?
Tamarind (Tamarindus indica) is a leguminous tree bearing edible fruit that is indigenous to tropical Africa and naturalized in Asia.
The largest member of the genus Panthera and an apex predator of Asian forests, this big cat wears orange fur striped in mostly-vertical black — what is it?
Tiger (Panthera tigris) is a large cat and a member of the genus Panthera native to Asia.
Nicknamed carbamide, this is the simplest amide of carbamic acid: two amino groups joined by a single carbonyl, and the body's chief way of shedding nitrogen in urine. What compound is it?
Urea (because it is a diamide of carbonic acid), is an organic compound with chemical formula CO(NH2)2.
He co-developed the V-2 at Peenemünde — the first artificial object to cross the Kármán line into space — before bringing his rocketry to the United States; who was this engineer?
Wernher von Braun (23 March 1912 - 16 June 1977) was a German American aerospace engineer and space architect.
Named for its standard passenger capacity, this twin-engine turboprop regional airliner is assembled in Toulouse by a Franco-Italian manufacturer that is half-owned by Airbus — what aircraft is this?
ATR 72: Regional turboprop airliner. The ATR 72 is a twin-engine turboprop, short-haul regional airliner developed and produced in France and Italy by aircraft manufacturer ATR.
Sold as button, cremini, or portobello depending on its stage of maturity, this cultivated mushroom is grown in more than 70 countries — what species is it?
Agaricus bisporus: Species of fungus. Agaricus bisporus, commonly known as the cultivated mushroom, is a basidiomycete mushroom native to grasslands in Eurasia and North America.
Meaning 'different lizard' and first described in 1877 by Othniel Marsh, most fossils of this Late Jurassic predator come from North America's Morrison Formation — which dinosaur?
This Manchester physicist shared the 2010 Nobel Prize for his work on graphene — and is the only person to also hold an Ig Nobel, won for levitating a frog with magnetism. Who is he?
In this severe blood disorder, the bone marrow stops producing red cells, white cells and platelets alike, and about half of all cases have no known cause — what condition is it?
Aplastic anemia: Disease causing insufficient blood cells of all types.

Often called a 'collapsed lung' in casual speech, this condition is really the partial deflation of the lung's alveoli rather than fluid filling them, and shows up frequently on chest X-rays — what is it?
Atelectasis: Partial collapse of a lung causing reduced gas exchange.
A tender herb of the mint family native from Central Africa to Southeast Asia, its Genovese or 'sweet' variety is a kitchen staple worldwide — what is it?
Basil: Culinary herb. Basil (Ocimum basilicum), also called great basil, is a culinary herb of the family Lamiaceae (mints).

Closely related to the beech-oak family and including species widespread across the Northern Hemisphere's temperate and boreal zones, which thin-leaved deciduous hardwood genus is prized for its versatile wood?
Birch: Genus of flowering plants in the family Betulaceae.
Holding the title of smallest great ape, this creature has pinker lips and a darker face than its close cousin, and was once dismissed as merely a 'pygmy' subspecies of it — what is it?
Bonobo: Species of great ape. Taxonomically, members of the chimpanzee/bonobo subtribe Panina—composed entirely by the genus Pan—are collectively termed panins.
Nicknamed 'the lawyer' and 'freshwater cod,' this coldwater fish is the only member of its genus and the sole freshwater species in its entire order — what fish is it?
Burbot: Species of fish. The species is closely related to marine fish such as the common ling and cusk, all of which belong to the family Lotidae (rocklings).
Also known as Flinders rose, this perennial shrub with rounded fleshy leaves and white-to-pink flowers is native across circum-Mediterranean countries — what's the plant called?
Marketed as a COX-2 inhibitor, this NSAID treats arthritis pain and menstrual cramps but carries heart attack and stroke risk warnings — which drug?
The only member of the onion genus native to both the New World and Old World, this perennial herb has edible leaves and flowers and doubles as a natural insect repellent — what is it?
Chives: Species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.

First discovered as an atypical antipsychotic, this medication is reserved for schizophrenia patients who haven't responded to two other drugs, and is also used for psychosis linked to Parkinson's disease — what is it?
Clozapine: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Clozapine, sold under the brand name Clozaril among others, is a psychiatric medication and was the first atypical antipsychotic to be discovered.
Named after a Quechua word meaning the same thing, this New World vulture — with Andean and Californian species — is the largest flying land bird in the Western Hemisphere. What is it?
Condor: Name for two species of vultures.
Commonly called comb jellies, these are the largest animals that swim using rows of cilia, drifting through every ocean as masses of two-layered jelly — what's the phylum?
Ctenophora: Phylum of gelatinous marine animals.
From muntjac to moose, members of the family Cervidae shed and regrow bony skull extensions each year — antlers used to battle rivals. What hoofed ruminant is this?
Deer: Family of hoofed mammals. A deer (pl.: deer) or true deer is a hoofed ruminant ungulate of the family Cervidae (informally the deer family).

He didn't just arrange the known elements — he left gaps and boldly predicted the properties of three undiscovered ones, later vindicated by germanium, gallium, and scandium. Which Russian chemist was he?
Having studied mathematics under Karl Weierstrass, which philosopher founded the school of phenomenology and argued that transcendental consciousness sets the limits of all possible knowledge?
Coiled to just 6 to 7 centimetres but stretching nearly 20 feet if unraveled, this tube connects each testicle to the vas deferens and stores maturing sperm — what is it?

Epididymis: Tube that connects a testicle to a vas deferens. The epididymis serves as an interconnection between the multiple efferent ducts at the rear of a testicle (proximally), and the vas deferens (distally).
The most widely distributed member of its subfamily, this semiaquatic, fish-eating mustelid ranges across Europe, much of Asia, and North Africa's Maghreb — which animal?
Made by nearly every living organism, this protein locks iron away in a safe, soluble form inside cells, and its blood level is the standard test doctors use for anemia or iron overload — what is it?
Ferritin: Iron-carrying protein. Ferritin is a universal intracellular and extracellular protein that stores iron and releases it in a controlled fashion.
As commander of Apollo 8, he led the first crew to circle the Moon and earned the Congressional Space Medal of Honor — who is he?
Frank Borman: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1928–2023)
Pioneered by Gregor Mendel's 19th-century pea plant experiments in Brno, this branch of biology studies heredity and trait inheritance — what is it?
Genetics: Science of genes, heredity and variation.

Weighing up to 175 grams, this South American tarantula is the world's most massive spider — despite a name inspired by an 18th-century engraving of one eating a hummingbird, it rarely actually preys on birds. Which species?
Goliath birdeater: Species of tarantula from South America.
A lentivirus and member of the retrovirus family, it gradually cripples the human immune system — and untreated, leaves roughly 9 to 11 years before the immune collapse called AIDS. What is it?
HIV: Human retrovirus, cause of AIDS. Without treatment, the average survival time after infection with HIV is estimated to be 9 to 11 years, depending on the HIV subtype.

This 19th-century American economist argued in his bestseller 'Progress and Poverty' that a single tax on land values could build a fairer, more productive society — sparking a movement named for him. Who was he?
An American aviator and aerospace engineer who first made his name as a big-budget Hollywood producer, this man grew famous late in life for his reclusive, eccentric ways — who was the magnate?
Howard Hughes: American aviator, aerospace engineer and business magnate (1905–1976)
This 14th-century Arab scholar wrote his most famous work, the Muqaddimah, in just six months and once met the conqueror Tamerlane — who is he?
Ibn Khaldun: Arab Islamic scholar, historian and philosopher (1332–1406)
Sold under the brand name Accutane, this vitamin A-related retinoid treats severe cystic acne but commonly causes dry lips, dry skin, and increased sunburn risk — what is it called?
Isotretinoin: Medication primarily used to treat severe acne.
In a landmark 1913 Columbia University address, this American psychologist championed behaviorism and later became known for the unsettling 'Little Albert' experiment — who is he?
In this eye disorder, the cornea gradually thins and bulges into a cone shape, causing blurry or double vision often linked to excessive eye rubbing as a risk factor — which condition?
Keratoconus: Medical condition involving the eye.
Described both as a science and as the art of justice, this set of enforced rules can be made by legislatures, executive decrees or judges' precedent — what is it?
Sold under the brand name Vyvanse, this prodrug of dextroamphetamine treats ADHD and moderate-to-severe binge eating disorder, taking effect within about 90 minutes — which medication?
Lisdexamfetamine: Central nervous system stimulant prodrug.

Fired by IBM in 1968 for revealing her intent to transition — an apology that took until 2020 — this computer scientist had already invented dynamic instruction handling behind modern out-of-order execution. Who was she?
Lynn Conway: American computer scientist and electrical engineer (1938–2024)
The second woman ever to win the Nobel Prize in Physics (after Marie Curie) shared the 1963 award for her discoveries about nuclear shell structure — who was she?

Encompassing conditions marked by a clinically significant disturbance in thinking, emotional regulation, or behavior that causes real distress or impaired functioning, this broad psychiatric category has causes that remain often unclear — what is the umbrella term for it?
This twin-engine Soviet fighter, known to NATO as 'Fulcrum,' was built in the 1970s to counter American jets like the F-15 and F-16 — which aircraft is it?
Mikoyan MiG-29: Soviet twin-engine jet fighter aircraft. The Mikoyan MiG-29 (Russian: Микоян МиГ-29; NATO reporting name: Fulcrum) is a twin-engine fighter aircraft designed in the Soviet Union.
This telecommunications method encodes text as standardised sequences of just two different signal durations. What are they called?
Morse code is a telecommunications method which encodes text characters as standardized sequences of two different signal durations, called dots and dashes, or dits and dahs.

The males of this stocky Arctic cetacean sport a spiralled 'tusk' up to three metres long — actually a protruding left canine tooth thought to work as a weapon, a tool, and maybe a salinity sensor. What animal is it?

Usually made from unleavened dough that's rolled, cut, or extruded into long strips, this staple food is called pasta in Italian cuisine and split into wheat-based and starch-based varieties in Chinese cooking — what is it?
Noodle: Staple food made from unleavened dough, commonly long and thin.
Discovered by naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace in 1859, this fungus hijacks carpenter ants' brains and marches them down to the forest floor before killing them — which organism?

Ophiocordyceps unilateralis: Species of fungus. Ophiocordyceps unilateralis, commonly known as zombie-ant fungus, is an insect-pathogenic fungus, discovered by the British naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace in 1859.
First domesticated in Mesoamerica and led in production today by India, this tropical fruit belongs to the small genus Carica — what is it?
Papaya: Species of tropical fruit plant.
This inflammation of the sac surrounding the heart causes sharp chest pain that eases when sitting up and worsens when lying down or breathing deeply — what condition is it?
Pericarditis: Inflammation of the pericardium. Pericarditis (PER-i-kar-DYE-tis) is inflammation of the pericardium, the fibrous sac surrounding the heart.
Boasting the longest cones of any spruce and widely planted as a Christmas tree, this European conifer was also the first gymnosperm to have its genome sequenced — which species?
Picea abies: Species of plant. Picea abies, the Norway spruce, Norway fir or European spruce, is a species of spruce native to Northern, Central and Eastern Europe.
Born Joseph Ratzinger, this head of the Catholic Church made history in 2013 by resigning the role, then adopted the title 'emeritus' until his death — who was he?
Pope Benedict XVI: Head of the Catholic Church from 2005 to 2013.

With 348 known species spanning an opportunistic human pathogen, a plant disease-causer, and a soil-dwelling growth-promoter, which gram-negative bacterial genus in Gammaproteobacteria is renowned for its metabolic diversity?
Pseudomonas: Genus of Gram-negative bacteria. Pseudomonas is a genus of gram-negative bacteria belonging to the family Pseudomonadaceae in the class Gammaproteobacteria.
This Norwegian shared the very first Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics, and we owe him the words 'econometrics,' 'microeconomics,' and 'macroeconomics' — who was he?
Ragnar Frisch: Norwegian economist and Nobel Laureate (1895–1973)
Native to Europe, northwestern Africa, and southwestern Asia, this flowering shrub's edible fruit stars in desserts and preserves — what's its species name, better known as the gooseberry?
Ribes uva-crispa: Species of flowering plant in the family Grossulariaceae.
Introduced in the 1970s, this database language let programmers grab many records with one single command, eliminating the need to specify an index path to reach each one — what is it?

Originally from the Mediterranean, this yellowish-gray arthropod has up to 15 pairs of long legs and preys on insects with venom too mild to harm humans — what species commonly invades homes worldwide?
Scutigera coleoptrata: Species of arthropod. Scutigera coleoptrata, also known as the house centipede, is a species of centipede that is typically yellowish-gray and has up to 15 pairs of long legs.
Better known by the brand name Viagra, this drug treats erectile dysfunction and pulmonary arterial hypertension, kicking in within about twenty minutes — what is it?

Sildenafil: Drug for erectile dysfunction and hypertension. Sildenafil, sold under the brand name Viagra among others, is a medication used to treat erectile dysfunction and pulmonary arterial hypertension.
Native to East Asia and the world's most-grown legume, this crop becomes everything from edamame and tofu to soy sauce, nattō and tempeh — what is it?
Soybean: Legume grown for its edible bean.
This throat infection causes fever, red tonsils, and swollen neck glands, and can trigger a sandpaper-textured rash known as scarlet fever — which condition?
Streptococcal pharyngitis: Medical condition. It may be spread directly through touching infected sores.

This mammal family includes true digging specialists as well as aquatic desmans and the water-and-tunnel-adept star-nosed species, absent from Ireland but found from Eurasia to as far south as tropical Southeast Asian mountains — which family?
Talpidae: Family of small insectivorous mammals.
A cousin of caffeine found in trace amounts in tea, coffee, and chocolate, which methylxanthine drug is used to treat asthma and COPD by blocking adenosine receptors?
Theophylline: Drug used to treat respiratory diseases.
This central part of the body, from which the head, neck, limbs, and tail extend, is divided into chest, abdomen, and pelvic segments — which body part?

Torso: Central part of the living body. The tetrapod torso — including that of a human — can be divided into segments:

The chest or upper torso.

A reddish-purple natural dye secreted by sea snails in the Muricidae family, also called royal purple or imperial dye. The colored compound is 6,6'-dibromoindigo, extracted from snails like Bolinus brandaris. What is this ancient dye?
Tyrian purple: Natural dye extracted from Murex sea snails. The name Tyrian refers to the city of Tyre in ancient Phoenicia (modern-day Lebanon).
Despite a scientific name meaning 'sand burrower,' this snake actually prefers rocky terrain and is considered Europe's most dangerous viper thanks to fangs up to 13mm long — which species?
Vipera ammodytes: Species of snake. It is reputed to be the most dangerous of the European vipers due to its large size, long fangs (up to 13 mm) and high venom toxicity.
In 1879 at the University of Leipzig, this German scholar founded the first formal psychology laboratory, earning him the title 'father of experimental psychology' — who is he?
Wilhelm Wundt: German founder of psychology (1832–1920)
Known on the street as flakka or gravel, this synthetic stimulant of the cathinone class was developed in the 1960s and later sold as a designer drug — what is it?
The symbol for iridium is Ir. Iridium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ir and atomic number 77.

Morena Baccarin: Morena Silva de Vaz Setta Baccarin (Brazilian Portuguese: [moˈɾenɐ bakaˈɾĩ]; born June 2, 1979) is an American actress.

Danny DeVito: Daniel Michael DeVito Jr., ( də-VEE-toh; born November 17, 1944) is an American actor and filmmaker.

Rajinikanth: Shivaji Rao Gaikwad (born 12 December 1950), known professionally as Rajinikanth, is an Indian actor who predominantly works in Tamil cinema.

Katrina Kaif (pronounced [kəˈʈriːna kɛːf]; born Katrina Rosemary Turcotte, 16 July 1983) is a British actress and businesswoman who works in Hindi-language films.
In what year did Ryan O'Neal die?
Ryan O'Neal: Charles Patrick Ryan O'Neal (April 20, 1941 – December 8, 2023) was an American actor.

In what year was The Banshees of Inisherin first released?
